from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A matrix transforms a vector in space.", "We can visualize this as grid morphing.", "Consider a rotation matrix applied to coordinates."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Transformation View", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize objects
        # Using SVG asset
        grid = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        grid.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'A4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        v1 = Vector([1, 0], color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        matrix_label = MathTex("A = \\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\\\ 1 & 0 \\end{pmatrix}", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_in_area(matrix_label, 'A4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(grid), Create(v1))
        self.play(Write(matrix_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Simple grid morph animation
        self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix(np.array([[0, -1], [1, 0]])),
                  v1.animate.apply_matrix(np.array([[0, -1], [1, 0]])))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Highlight basis vectors
        basis_i = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF4500")
        basis_j = Vector([0, 1], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_i, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_j, 'F4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_i), FadeIn(basis_j))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Order matters in matrix multiplication.",
            "Socks then shoes differs from shoes then socks.",
            "Multiplication tracks successive transformations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Order Sensitivity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # AB: Rotation then Scaling
        ab_label = Text("Result of AB", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        ab_square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        ab_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/socks.svg")
        ab_group = VGroup(ab_label, ab_square, ab_icon).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # BA: Scaling then Rotation
        ba_label = Text("Result of BA", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        ba_square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.3)
        ba_square.rotate(PI/4)
        ba_group = VGroup(ba_label, ba_square).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # Difference/Shoes icon
        shoes_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shoes.svg")
        diff_label = Text("Order Matters!", font_size=24, color="#FF4500")
        diff_group = VGroup(diff_label, shoes_icon).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(ab_group, 'B1', 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(ab_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_in_area(ba_group, 'B4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(ba_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(diff_group), Flash(diff_group))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Transformation View
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a function T(v) = Av that moves a vector in space. Visualize this as a 'grid morphing' animation where a matrix A stretches or rotates a 2D coordinate system.
sections.example: A 2D vector [1, 0] being mapped to [0, 1] by a rotation matrix.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition
sections.content: Explain that applying two transformations in sequence (T2 after T1) is equivalent to a single transformation. Define this as T(v) = T2(T1(v)). Use a 'Robot Arm' analogy where the first joint rotates and the second joint translates relative to the first.
sections.example: Robot Arm: Joint A rotates the base, Joint B rotates the forearm; the final position is a composition of both actions.

sections.title: Bridging to Matrix Multiplication
sections.content: Show mathematically that if T1(v) = Av and T2(u) = Bu, then T2(T1(v)) = B(Av) = (BA)v. Emphasize that the matrix BA represents the combined effect of A followed by B.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Stretch' matrix (A) followed by a 'Rotate' matrix (B), resulting in a single 'Spiral' matrix (BA).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Why': The Grid Perspective
sections.content: Use an animation showing a unit square. Step 1: Apply matrix A (shearing). Step 2: Apply matrix B to the result. Show that the final grid matches applying the single matrix product (BA) directly to the original square.
sections.example: A square being sheared by matrix A and then flipped by matrix B, showing the final state equals the product BA.

sections.title: Summary & Order Sensitivity
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting why BA does not usually equal AB. Just like putting on socks then shoes is different from shoes then socks, the order of transformations matters. Reinforce that matrix multiplication is simply the 'bookkeeping' for successive transformations.
sections.example: A 2D character sprite: Rotating then Scaling looks different than Scaling then Rotating.
